title: Overcoming beta-agonist tolerance: high dose salbutamol and ipratropium bromide. Two randomised controlled trials
population: Adults with asthma in New Zealand; two double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover studies of 11 subjects each, with inhaled formoterol 12 µg twice daily for one week
funder: The study was funded by the Waikato Respiratory Research Fund. Competing interests: the authors declare that they have no competing interests.
result: Thirty-six hours after the last dose of one week of formoterol 12 µg twice daily or placebo, bronchoconstriction was induced and a bronchodilator given. The response to 5 mg nebulised salbutamol after methacholine challenge was 15% lower after formoterol than after placebo (95% CI 5 to 25%, p = 0.008) in 11 subjects. In a second group of 11 subjects challenged with 4.5% saline, the response to ipratropium bromide 40 µg was unchanged.
